displayedInputs.question: If a line is parallel to a plane, what can be said about its direction?

choices.A: It must be perpendicular to the plane
choices.B: It has the same direction as a family of parallel lines of intersection in the plane
choices.C: It must pass through the plane
choices.D: It cannot be parallel to any line in the plane

displayedInputs.question: Two intersecting lines in plane \(\alpha\) are both parallel to plane \(\beta\). What follows?

choices.B: \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are perpendicular
choices.C: We can only conclude that a line is parallel to a plane

displayedInputs.question: If only one line in a plane is parallel to another plane, can we conclude that the two planes are parallel?

choices.B: Yes
choices.C: Only if this line is a lateral edge

displayedInputs.question: How many intersecting lines in the plane does the criterion require as references?

The parallel-plane criterion states that if two intersecting lines in plane \(\alpha\) are each parallel to plane \(\beta\), then \(\alpha\) is parallel to \(\beta\). Suppose instead that two distinct parallel lines in \(\alpha\) are each parallel to \(\beta\). What follows?

choices.A: We can still conclude that the two planes are parallel
choices.B: The two planes must be perpendicular
choices.C: This criterion cannot be applied directly

displayedInputs.question: When two parallel planes are cut by a third plane, what can be said about the two resulting lines of intersection?

choices.A: They are parallel to each other
choices.B: They are perpendicular to each other

displayedInputs.question: If two planes are parallel, what is the relationship between a line in one plane and the other plane?

choices.B: It lies in the other plane
choices.C: It is parallel to the other plane
choices.D: It is perpendicular to the other plane

displayedInputs.question: When two planes are parallel, how many points do they have in common?

choices.B: Infinitely many points on a line

displayedInputs.question: Line \(l\) is perpendicular to two intersecting lines in a plane. What follows?

choices.A: \(l\) is only parallel to the plane
choices.B: \(l\) is perpendicular to this plane
choices.D: We cannot yet determine the relationship

displayedInputs.question: If a line is perpendicular to only one line in a plane, can we conclude that it is perpendicular to the plane?

choices.B: Yes, if this line passes through the center of the circle

displayedInputs.question: In the criterion theorem, how many intersecting lines in the plane are required?
What is the relationship between two lines perpendicular to the same plane?

choices.B: They must be skew
choices.C: They are parallel to each other

displayedInputs.question: If a line is perpendicular to a plane, what is it perpendicular to?

choices.B: Only two lines

displayedInputs.question: What relationship between two lines is the conclusion of the property theorem?

choices.B: Parallel

displayedInputs.question: If one plane contains a line perpendicular to another plane, what is the relationship between the two planes?

choices.A: They are parallel to each other
choices.B: They must coincide
choices.D: They are perpendicular to each other

displayedInputs.question: How are a wall and a floor usually modeled geometrically?

choices.B: Two skew lines

displayedInputs.question: You want to determine the service life of a batch of light bulbs, but cannot use up all the bulbs. Which approach is more appropriate?

choices.B: Conduct a census of all the light bulbs
choices.C: Ask only one person for their impression

displayedInputs.question: Looking up population data already published by the statistics bureau is an example of what?

choices.B: Consulting existing information

displayedInputs.question: A class has 40 students. If a census is conducted, how many students must data be collected from?
What must first be clarified before obtaining data?

choices.B: Calculate the variance first

displayedInputs.question: A population consists of 20 people, and 1 person is selected by simple random sampling. What is the probability that each person is selected?
A simple random sample of 2 items is selected from a population of 10 items. How many different selections are possible?
What does simple random sampling require?

choices.A: Select only students with good grades
choices.B: Sample in proportion to class sizes
choices.C: The sample must equal the population
choices.D: Each individual has the same probability of being selected

displayedInputs.question: In the lottery method, what should be done with the numbers?

choices.B: Arrange them in ascending order and select only those at the front
choices.D: Repeatedly select the same person until satisfied

displayedInputs.question: Stratum A has 40 people and stratum B has 60 people. Stratified sampling is conducted at a rate of \(1/10\). How many people should be selected from stratum A?
Stratum A has 40 people and stratum B has 60 people. Stratified sampling is performed at a sampling fraction of \(1/10\). How many people should be sampled from stratum B?
Stratum A has 40 people and stratum B has 60 people. A stratified random sample selects \(1/10\) of each stratum. What is the combined sample size for the two strata?
When is stratified sampling appropriate?

choices.B: The population consists of several distinctly different strata
choices.C: Every individual is exactly the same
choices.D: Continuous production that cannot be divided into groups

displayedInputs.question: The numbers of students in a school's three grade levels differ greatly. To investigate the daily time spent on homework across the school, which method is more appropriate?

choices.A: Sample from only one grade level
choices.B: Combine the three grade levels without considering their numbers of students

displayedInputs.question: There are 20 fountain pens in the same box, with no information for stratification other than their appearance. Which method should be used to sample 4 pens for inspection?

choices.B: Stratification is required

displayedInputs.question: A sample size of 8 does not mean that the population contains only 8 individuals. If the population size is 80, what fraction of the population size is the sample size?
Which statement describes the result of an inference based on a sample?

choices.A: It must equal the population parameter
choices.B: It cannot be used to make any judgments
choices.C: It is an estimate and does not necessarily equal the exact population value
choices.D: It applies only to the people in the sample and is unrelated to the population

displayedInputs.question: The class width is 5, the relative frequency divided by the class width equals 0.04, and the sample size is 50. What is the frequency count for this class?
The relative frequencies of two classes are 0.3 and 0.7, respectively. What is the sum of the relative frequencies?
The class width is 10, the frequency count for a class is 20, and the sample size is 100. Divide this class's relative frequency by the class width and express the result as a fraction.
What does the height of a rectangle in the histogram represent?

choices.B: The sample size
choices.D: Relative frequency divided by class width

displayedInputs.question: The sample size is 40, and the relative frequency of a class is 0.25. What is the frequency count for this class?
Class A has a relative frequency of 0.2, and class B has a relative frequency of 0.35. By how much does the relative frequency of class B exceed that of class A?
The sample size is 80. How many data values are in a class with a relative frequency of \(1/5\)?
In a histogram with equal class widths, what does a taller rectangle indicate?

choices.A: This class has a greater relative frequency
choices.B: The data values in this class are smaller
